_comment: Machine-readable licence gate for the Stage A corpus (§7.3). `training/scripts/fetch_corpus.py` refuses to download anything whose licence is not verified here, and `--verify` is the only way to set that flag: it requires the SPDX id, the URL that was actually read, and who verified it. Nothing in this file is enabled today — the seed fixture in data/raw/seed is generated by training/scripts/make_seed_corpus.py and is ours.

policy.rule: A source may be fetched only when license.verified is true AND enabled is true. There is no --force flag: an unverified source is a decision that has not been made, and a training run that stops for a decision is cheaper than a model trained on text we had no right to use.
policy.record: Each verification records spdx, url, verified_by and verified_at so docs/DATA_LICENSES.md can be reconciled against this file by a test.
policy.licence_classes: A verified licence can still be one we may not use. NC (NonCommercial) and ND (NoDerivatives) are refused by default because a distributed model in a professional portfolio is not a personal, non-commercial use. Matching is token-wise, so NCSA is not NC.
policy.provenance: docs/DATA_LICENSES.md rule 1: no third-party LLM-generated dataset may be used unless its provenance is recorded and disclosed. Every source states `provenance.origin` (human | web | synthetic | own-work), and a `synthetic` source cannot be fetched without a `disclosure` string explaining where it must be admitted.

_observed_comment: `license.observed` is research: someone looked up the terms and wrote down what they found, with the page they found it on. It is deliberately NOT `verified` — only a named person asserts that, per the rule above. A source may be observed and still unfetchable.

sources.name: AI4Bharat Sangraha (verified subset)
sources.why: Large, curated Hindi (Devanagari) text — the main Stage A source for Hindi prose.

provenance.notes: Curated by AI4Bharat from public web sources; not machine-generated.

observed.notes: Permissive: commercial use allowed with attribution. Usable if the owner confirms. Still needs a pinned revision before fetching — a CC-BY grant is not a revision.

license.notes: Terms must be read at the dataset page and the subset's own terms recorded. Confirm redistribution constraints: the model is a derivative, and data/ is git-ignored so no text is redistributed.

sources.notes: Download via huggingface_hub with a pinned revision; record the revision hash in the fetch manifest.

sources.name: Hindi Wikipedia dump
sources.why: Broad Hindi prose with an unambiguous licence.

observed.quote: the spdx and url above were already recorded in this file; the page itself was not re-fetched during this pass
observed.notes: ShareAlike is not NonCommercial, so it is not blocked by class. The open question is attribution: the corpus we build is a derivative and must be credited, and the dump stays out of the repository.

license.notes: Read 2026-09-30 on the owner's instruction; the Wikimedia legal page states all original textual content is licensed under CC BY-SA 4.0 and that Wikimedia content may be used for any purpose including commercial. Attribution applies to the corpus we build; the dump stays out of the repo. Operational: record the dump date and a revision id at fetch time, which is what makes the attribution reproducible.

sources.notes: Needs aggressive filtering: encyclopedic register, templated boilerplate, names, dates, and long lists of numerals.

sources.name: L3Cube-HingCorpus (Roman code-mixed)
sources.why: Real human Roman Hinglish, which programmatic data cannot reproduce.

provenance.notes: Human-written Twitter posts. Genuinely human, which was its whole appeal.

observed.confidence: high that it is NonCommercial; medium on the exact id
observed.quote: L3Cube-HingCorpus, and L3Cube-HingLID is licensed under a Creative Commons Attribution-NonCommercial-ShareAlike 4.0 International License
observed.notes: BLOCKED BY CLASS. Two sources agree it is NonCommercial (the project README, and the LREC/WILDRE proceedings). They disagree on the variant — the README says CC-BY-NC-SA-4.0, the proceedings PDF says CC-BY-NC-4.0 — so the exact id needs the owner's check before anything else. Either way it cannot enter a distributed model while allow_noncommercial is false. This is the finding the executable gate exists to surface: the licence was on the 'must check' list, and checking it changed the answer.

license.notes: Twitter-derived. Licence check is mandatory AND the PII/toxicity/URL filtering burden is the highest of any candidate.

sources.notes: High conversational noise. If used, cap its share of the training mixture and report the share. As observed, it is not usable: see license.observed. The Roman Hinglish gap this was meant to fill is a real loss — programmatic data cannot reproduce human code-mixing, so Stage A's Hinglish will be weaker, and that limitation belongs in the model card rather than being papered over with data we may not use.

sources.name: TinyStories
sources.why: §7.3's 'narrow, clean distribution' taken literally: short simple narratives whose vocabulary a small model can actually learn. The paper's whole finding is that 1–30M-parameter models are coherent on it.

provenance.disclosure: This corpus is entirely machine-generated and must be named as such in the dataset card and the model card. The licence is permissive; the provenance rule is what applies here, and it applies to the *model* the owner ships, not only to the training run.

observed.notes: Not NonCommercial and not NoDerivatives, so not blocked by class. CDLA-Sharing is a data licence: it obliges sharing improvements to the *dataset*, not to a model trained on it. The live question is the synthetic provenance above, not the licence.

license.notes: The dataset's own metadata file (raw README.md on main) states 'license: cdla-sharing-1.0' verbatim; the card URL is above. Not NC and not ND, so the licence passes. It is entirely GPT-3.5/GPT-4 output, so DATA_LICENSES rule 1 applies and the disclosure field is the load-bearing one, not the licence.

sources.notes: Bounded vocabulary and narrative register — good for fluency, useless for the portfolio Q&A that Stage B handles. Cap its share and report it.

sources.name: Simple English Wikipedia dump
sources.why: Simple, clean English prose written for a reduced vocabulary — the closest thing to §7.3's 'narrow, clean distribution' that is also real-world text.

provenance.notes: Human-written. Some articles are LLM-assisted by their authors; the dump does not mark them, which is a known limitation of any Wikipedia-derived corpus.

observed.quote: published under both the Creative Commons Attribution/Share-Alike License 4.0 International License and the GNU Free Documentation License
observed.notes: Same terms as the Hindi dump: not NC, so not blocked by class; attribution obligations apply to the corpus we build.

license.notes: Same page and the same terms as the Hindi dump: dumps.wikimedia.org/legal.html covers all Wikimedia text, so CC BY-SA 4.0 applies to simplewiki. Attribution obligations fall on the corpus.

sources.notes: Record the dump date and revision; the dump stays out of the repository.

sources.name: Topical-Chat (Alexa Prize)
sources.why: Human-human open-domain conversation with clean speaker turns — everyday English dialogue, which Wikipedia cannot supply.

provenance.notes: Human-human conversations collected through Amazon Mechanical Turk. Not machine-generated.

observed.quote: AWS Open Data entry lists License: CDLA-Sharing
observed.notes: The CDLA-Sharing id came from the AWS registry entry for the *enriched* Topical-Chat. Whether the enrichment carries the same terms as the base corpus is unconfirmed, so this needs the owner's read. Not NC either way.

license.notes: Confirmed to belong to a different licence family from DailyDialog, which is the point of checking.

sources.notes: Acquisition channel not chosen: register it as 'local' once attached as a Kaggle input, or as 'http_file' with a pinned URL. No URL is invented here.

sources.name: DailyDialog
sources.why: The canonical high-quality multi-turn everyday-dialogue corpus, and the first thing anyone reaches for when asked for 'simple English dialogue'.

provenance.notes: Human-written dialogues by English learners, which is why the language is simple.

observed.quote: DailyDialog dataset is licensed under CC BY-NC-SA 4.0
observed.notes: BLOCKED BY CLASS. Multiple independent mirrors and the dataset's own loader state NonCommercial, so this is not ambiguous the way L3Cube's variant was. Dropped on the same grounds.

license.notes: If the terms are ever revised by the authors, re-run --verify; until then this entry records a decision that was made, not one that is pending.

sources.notes: Recorded so nobody re-researches it: the most obvious choice for this slot is the one we may not use.

sources.name: PersonaChat
sources.why: Persona-grounded chit-chat. Considered as a fallback for the dialogue slot.

observed.quote: a Kaggle mirror states CC BY-NC-SA 4.0; the ParlAI project page states no data licence
observed.notes: INCONCLUSIVE, and deliberately left that way. A mirror's licence claim is not the rights-holder's grant, and the original release does not plainly state one. NonCommercial would block it; MIT would not. Do not resolve this by picking the convenient mirror — go to the source, or drop it.

license.notes: An inconclusive licence check is a result worth recording: it stops the same hour being spent twice and it stops the convenient answer being assumed.

sources.notes: Not carried further. Only pursued if the dialogue slot still needs filling after Topical-Chat is confirmed.

sources.name: Portfolio-derived instruction data (Stage B)
sources.why: §7.4 Stage B: templates × paraphrases × three languages, plus counterfactual contexts and abstention examples.

provenance.notes: Generated from the owner's own knowledge base by our own script.

license.notes: Generated from the owner's own knowledge base; only public:true facts carry values, and URLs/emails become placeholders (§8.4 layer 3).

sources.notes: Enabled 2026-09-30 for the P4 Kaggle run. The previous note said 'the generator does not exist yet' while this very entry named it in `generator` two fields above — the file was describing a state that had already changed. Stage B is what makes the model answer inside the runtime chat frame, and this data is generated from the owner's own knowledge base, so nothing outside the project is involved. No `observed` block: there is no third-party page to read, which is the point of generating it.
